name: Extended-stay hotel
summary: All-suite extended-stay hotel (midscale, e.g., economy/midscale studio brands, through upscale, e.g., Residence Inn / Homewood class) with in-room kitchens and minimal public space. Larger rooms but low public-space ratio make cost per SF lower than select-service; midscale and upscale segments differ by ~60–70% per key, so the default blends them. HVS reports both segments separately for four survey years, giving solid national data.

typicalSize.method: HCEG extended-stay prototype: 150 guestrooms, 4 stories (e24); midscale extended-stay prototypes are commonly ~100–125 keys. Mid 120.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: HCEG extended-stay studio 548 SF incl. kitchen plus 12x8 bath (96 SF) ≈ 640 SF net (upscale) (e25); with ~0.80–0.85 guestroom share (little public space) → ~750–800 GSF/key for upscale. Midscale studios are ~300–350 SF net → ~450–500 GSF/key. Mid 650 blends the two.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: 3–4 story buildings of ~80,000 GSF on 2–3 acres with ~1 surface space per key; derived from footprint + parking arithmetic.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: HCEG extended-stay prototype: 175 spaces for 150 rooms = 1.17 (e26); long-stay guests mostly drive.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS building & site improvements per key (median / average): upscale ES 2025 data $190,694 / $170,172 (e1), 2024 data $178,972 / $201,549 (e3), 2023 data $168,322 / $176,045 (e5); midscale ES 2025 data $110,057 / $111,724 (e2), 2024 data $113,958 / $116,160 (e4), 2023 data $109,368 / $109,126 (e6). Segment midpoint ≈ $148k; x0.91 (remove permits, engineering, hard contingency included by HVS) → $135k. Low $95k ≈ 0.91 x midscale ES (~$110k) less a small discount for 3-story wood/economy builds; high $200k ≈ 0.91 x upscale ES 2024 average ($183k) plus metro premium (RLB 3-star metro median-of-lows $343/SF x 650 SF ≈ $223k, e7).

perSF.method: Mid = $135k ÷ 650 SF ≈ $208/SF. Low ≈ $95k ÷ ~600 SF (midscale rooms are smaller, so $/SF does not fall as fast as $/key); high ≈ RLB 2026 metro 3-star median of lows ($343/SF, e7); Phoenix 3-star $230–$350 (e8).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC and OH&P and typical on-site work; includes in-suite kitchen cabinetry/countertops (carved out below); excludes kitchen appliances (in FF&E), land, soft costs, pre-opening, permits, contingency, off-sites, impact/tap fees, financing.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ midscale ES / blend ($110k / $148k ≈ 0.74, e2); premium ≈ upscale ES / blend ($191k / $148k ≈ 1.3, e1); luxury = high/mid ($200k / $135k ≈ 1.5).

systemSplit.method: Derived from the select-service split (same wood-frame low-rise construction) with +1 pt casework (12, in-suite kitchens) and +1 pt plumbing (22, kitchen sinks/dishwashers), offset by −1 pt finishes (09, less public space) and −1 pt metals (05).

lineItems.name: In-suite kitchen cabinetry and countertops

cost.method: HCEG 2021 extended-stay kitchen cabinetry $2,875–$4,500 per key (avg $3,840) (e27) x1.18 for the GC markups the guide excludes.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline hard cost.

lineItems.name: In-suite kitchen appliances (fridge, cooktop, microwave, dishwasher)

cost.method: HCEG 2021 extended-stay kitchen appliances $1,715–$2,345 per key (avg $2,066) (e28) x1.18 install/markup.

lineItems.notes: Normally carried in FF&E (HVS FF&E includes kitchen equipment) — switch on only if your FF&E budget excludes appliances.

lineItems.name: Pre-opening, OS&E and working capital

cost.method: HVS pre-opening & working capital per key: upscale ES 2025 data $4,863 median / $6,628 avg (e17); midscale ES $2,419 / $3,430 (e18); upscale ES 2024 data $5,100 / $5,622 (e19). Mid blends segments.

lineItems.notes: Owner cost incl. OS&E (kitchenware packages add to OS&E vs. select-service).

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS FF&E per key: upscale ES 2025 data $25,661 median / $24,361 avg (e9), 2024 data $20,796 / $23,253 (e11); midscale ES $16,594 (e10) and $17,032 (e12). Mid ≈ blend of segments.

pctOfHard.method: HVS soft ÷ building & site improvements (medians): upscale ES 2025 data 19,165/190,694 = 10.1% (e13), 2024 data 26,415/178,972 = 14.8% (e15); midscale ES 16,127/110,057 = 14.7% (e14), 17,213/113,958 = 15.1% (e16). Prototype-driven design keeps soft costs lowest of the hotel types. Financing (in HVS soft) and permits/engineering (in HVS building) roughly offset.

softCosts.notes: Includes A/E (prototype adaptation), brand application/technical-services fees (HVS lists the franchise application fee under soft costs), legal, insurance, permits, testing. Developer fee and financing handled separately.

hard.method: Typical new-construction hard-cost contingency for repetitive wood-frame hotels.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS all-in totals less land: midscale ES 2025 data $169,901 − $11,886 ≈ $158k median (e21), 2024 data ≈ $157k (e23); upscale ES 2025 data $264,841 − $18,182 ≈ $247k (e20), 2024 data average $286,237 − $21,602 ≈ $265k (e22). Totals include FF&E, pre-opening, financing and developer fee.

openQuestions: Default blends midscale and upscale extended-stay; consider splitting into two types (costs differ ~65% per key).
Need a brand prototype GSF/key for midscale extended-stay to firm up $/SF.
